raw_record.question_text: Find the measure of $\angle 1$ if $m\angle DGF = 53$ and $m\angle AGC = 40$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing triangle DGF, with F lying on the straight top segment DA and a right-angle mark at F showing DF ⟂ FG. Angle 1 is the angle at D between DG and DA, which is the same as ∠GDF because F is on DA. From the text, m∠DGF = 53. In right triangle DGF, the two acute angles sum to 90, so ∠GDF = 90 - 53 = 37. Therefore angle 1 measures 37.

method.method_draft: Use a fuller angle chase through the parallel horizontal segments. From the image, FG is perpendicular to both DA at F and GC at G, so DA ∥ GC. Also GA lies between GF and GC at G, and angle 1 is the angle at D of triangle DGA. From the text, m∠AGC = 40, so because ∠FGC is right, m∠FGA = 90 - 40 = 50. From the text, m∠DGF = 53, so the angle at G of triangle DGA is ∠DGA = ∠DGF + ∠FGA = 53 + 50 = 103. Since DA ∥ GC, transversal GA gives ∠DAG = ∠AGC = 40. Then in triangle DGA, angle 1 = ∠ADG = 180 - 103 - 40 = 37.
